problem: The position $x$ of a particle at time $t$ is given by $x(t)=\operatorname{ln}⁡({t}^{2}+1).$ Calculate the velocity at time $t.$

feedback.problem:
The position $s(t)$ of a particle (in feet) at time $t$ seconds is given by 

$$
s(t)=3{e}^{-t}+3\operatorname{ln}⁡t-3t,\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the speed of the particle when $t=3\,\text{s}.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{e}^{-t}+3\operatorname{ln}⁡t-3t) \\  & =-3{e}^{-t}+\frac{3}{t}-3\end{aligned}
$$

When $t=3,$ the velocity is

$$
\begin{aligned}v(3) & =-3{e}^{-3}+\frac{3}{3}-3 \\  & =-3{e}^{-3}-2 \\  & ≈-2.15\,\text{ft/s}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the speed is $|-2.15|=2.15\,\text{ft/s}.$
